claims.text: The target nanoparticles have diameters of 5–20 nm.
The target alloy contains five transition metals at approximately 20 at% each.
The initial nanoparticles form a single-phase FCC or BCC solid solution.
Elevated-temperature structural stability is governed by competition between configurational-entropy stabilization and surface-energy-driven segregation.
The component with the lowest surface energy segregates preferentially to the nanoparticle surface.
Surface segregation produces an enriched shell and a compositionally depleted core.
Formation of the core-shell structure accelerates atomic diffusion relative to bulk counterparts.
Accelerated nanoparticle diffusion violates the sluggish-diffusion assumption attributed to bulk high-entropy alloys.
A high surface-to-volume ratio induces a chemical-potential gradient that drives surface segregation.
The segregated shell and depleted core lower the activation energy for vacancy-mediated diffusion.
At moderate temperatures, the nanoparticle surface thermodynamic driving force overrides configurational-entropy stabilization.
The segregation-induced composition gradient enhances atomic mobility and can promote phase separation or amorphization.
In bulk high-entropy alloys, high configurational entropy stabilizes a single-phase solid solution and suppresses phase separation.
Severe lattice distortion causes sluggish diffusion in bulk high-entropy alloys.
Annealed nanoparticles will exhibit diffusion coefficients one to two orders of magnitude above values predicted by bulk HENA models.
Annealing may form intermetallic precipitates or amorphous phases that are absent in corresponding bulk samples.
The hypothesis fails above a particle diameter of 50 nm because surface effects become negligible.
The hypothesis fails when component surface-energy differences are below 0.1 J/m².
Below 0.2 Tm, diffusion is kinetically frozen and the proposed instability will not occur.
The transition between entropy-dominated and segregation-dominated behavior depends on the particular elements, including whether refractory metals such as W or Mo are present.
